paper.title: An Efficient Algorithm for Thresholding Monte Carlo Tree Search

settings.name_in_paper: Thresholding Monte Carlo Tree Search problem (fixed confidence)
unmapped: Arms are the leaves of a known MAX/MIN-labelled game tree; the answer is whether the minimax value of the root is at least a known threshold theta
The learner knows the tree structure, node labels and the threshold theta
settings.definition_quote: Given a question tree $\mathcal{T}$ and its internal node label function $L$, at each round $t=1,2,\dots$, the player selects one leaf node $I(t) \in \mathcal{L}(\mathcal{T})$, and observes a reward $r(t)$ drawn from an unknown distribution with mean $\mu_{I(t)}$. In this paper, we assume that the distributions belong to a one-parameter exponential family... The player's task is to determine whether the root node $s_0$ is a winning or losing node.

settings.name_in_paper: Good action identification (GAI) problem on a MAX-rooted tree
unmapped: Arms are leaves of a known MAX/MIN game tree with MAX root; answer is any child of the root with minimax value >= theta, or 'no good action'
The learner knows the tree structure, node labels and the threshold theta
settings.definition_quote: A natural question is to ask whether our framework can be applied to find a good action at the root node $s_0$ with $L(s_0) = \text{`MAX'}$, i.e., the child node whose value is at least $\theta$. We call this problem the good action identification (GAI) problem

algorithms.name: Any GLR-stopping algorithm whose sampling proportions converge a.s. to the optimal weights (e.g. D-Tracking, C-Tracking)

tuning: GLR stopping rule with threshold beta(t,delta) of Eq. (betadef)

source.label: cor:kaufmann_prop15
source.quote: Any algorithm for Problem~\ref{prob:def} using the GLR stopping rule with the sequence of thresholds $(\beta(t,\delta))_{t\in \mathbb{N}}$ defined by Eq.~(\ref{eq:betadef}) ensures \[ \mathbb{P}(\tau_{\delta}<\infty,a_{s_0}(\hat{\bm{\mu}}(\tau_{\delta}))\neq a_{s_0}(\bm{\mu}))\le \delta. \]

results.notes: delta-correctness; stated as corollary of Kaufmann & Koolen 2021 Prop. 15 applied to this problem. Holds for any sampling rule, including RD-Tracking-TMCTS.

symbols.d_s0: optimal value max_w inf_{lambda in Alt(mu)} sum_l w_l d(mu_l, lambda_l), computed recursively over the tree

conditions: sampling rule ensures N_l(t)/t -> w^{s_0}_l(mu) almost surely for every leaf
tuning: GLR stopping rule with threshold beta(t,delta) of Eq. (betadef)

source.label: thm:as_upper_bound
source.quote: Using GLR stopping rule with the threshold $\beta(t,\delta)$ defined by Eq.~(\ref{eq:betadef}), and any sampling rule ensuring that for every leaf $\ell \in \mathcal{L}(T)$, $N_\ell(t) / t$ converges almost surely to $w^{s_0}_\ell(\bm{\mu})$, any algorithm for Problem~\ref{prob:def} guarantees that for all $\delta \in (0,1)$, $\mathbb{P}(\tau_\delta < +\infty) = 1$ and \[ \mathbb{P}_{\bm{\mu}} \left( \limsup_{\delta \to 0} \frac{\tau_\delta}{\log(1 / \delta)} \leq \frac{1}{d_{s_0}(\bm{\mu})} \right) = 1. \]

symbols.d_s0: optimal value max_w inf_{lambda in Alt(mu)} sum_l w_l d(mu_l, lambda_l), computed recursively over the tree

tuning: GLR stopping rule with threshold beta(t,delta) of Eq. (betadef)

source.quote: Using the threshold sequence $(\beta(t,\delta))_{t\in \mathbb{N}}$ defined by Eq.~(\ref{eq:betadef}), RD-Tracking-TMCTS guarantees that for all $\delta \in (0,1)$, $\mathbb{P}(\tau_\delta < +\infty) = 1$ and \[ \mathbb{P}_{\bm{\mu}} \left( \limsup_{\delta \to 0} \frac{\tau_\delta}{\log(1 / \delta)} \leq \frac{1}{d_{s_0}(\bm{\mu})} \right) = 1. \]

results.notes: Per-round time O(D log K) (Theorem 5.8), D tree depth, K max branching.

symbols.d_s0: optimal value max_w inf_{lambda in Alt(mu)} sum_l w_l d(mu_l, lambda_l), computed recursively over the tree

tuning: GLR stopping rule with threshold beta(t,delta) of Eq. (betadef)

source.label: thm:sample_complexity
source.quote: For RD-Tracking-TMCTS with the threshold sequence $(\beta(t,\delta))_{t\in \mathbb{N}}$ defined by Eq.~(\ref{eq:betadef}), expected stopping time $\mathbb{E}_{\bm{\mu}}[\tau_\delta]$ is asymptotically upper-bounded by \[ \limsup_{\delta \to +0} \frac{\mathbb{E}_{\bm{\mu}}[\tau_\delta]}{\log(1 / \delta)} \leq \frac{1}{ d_{s_0}(\bm{\mu})}. \]

results.notes: Matches the Garivier-Kaufmann lower bound (asymptotically optimal). Per-round time O(D log K) (Theorem 5.8).

symbols.d_s0: optimal value of the thresholding (decision) problem characteristic, max_w inf_{lambda in Alt(mu)} sum_l w_l d(mu_l, lambda_l)

conditions: root node is a MAX node
tuning: GAI GLR stopping rule Z^GAI_{s_0}(t) >= beta(t,delta)

source.label: thm:sample_complexity_GAI
source.quote: The algorithm obtained by replacing the stopping condition of Algorithm~\ref{alg:proposed} (line~\ref{line:stopping_condition}) with $Z^\mathrm{GAI}_{s_0}(t) \geq \beta(t,\delta)$ satisfies \[\limsup_{\delta \to +0} \frac{ \mathbb{E}[\tau_\delta] }{\log(1 / \delta)} \leq \frac{1}{d_{s_0}(\bm{\mu})}.\]

results.notes: Paper claims the GAI lower bound (Degenne & Koolen) is lower bounded by d_s0^{-1}, making this optimal.

conditions: root node is a MAX node

source.quote: The algorithm obtained by replacing the stopping rule of Algorithm~\ref{alg:proposed} (line~\ref{line:stopping_condition}) with $Z^\mathrm{GAI}_{s_0}(t) \geq \beta(t,\delta)$ satisfies \[ \mathbb{P}(\tau_\delta < \infty, \hat{a}^\mathrm{GAI}(\tau_\delta) \text{ is not a correct answer}) \leq \delta\]
